title: Make appliance power type explicit instead of string-sniffed
description:
The single biggest trap for bring-your-own catalogs, and the reason this is P1 within the epic: it fails SILENTLY.

_infer_power_type (ccesim/device.py:73-84) decides solar vs mains by lowercasing the appliance's free-text 'type' field and looking for 'solar' or 'sdd'. That works on the packaged E003 rows because they happen to be worded that way. It does not work on anything a user writes themselves:

  type: 'Solar direct drive refrigerator'  -> solar   (correct)
  type: 'Refrigerator (photovoltaic)'      -> MAINS   (wrong, and silent)
  type: 'SDD fridge'                       -> solar   (correct, by luck)

A wrong answer here is not cosmetic. It selects the entire power model: no icebank behaviour, no solar bell curve, wrong holdover, wrong alarm profile. The user gets plausible-looking data that models the wrong appliance, with nothing in the output indicating it.

FIX: add an optional explicit power_type field ('solar' | 'mains') on appliance records. When present it wins. When absent, keep the existing string sniff so unmodified E003 exports still work. Consider logging at INFO when the sniff is what decided it, so the fallback is at least visible.

Populate power_type explicitly on the packaged appliance catalog rather than leaving the defaults on the sniff path.

Tests: an appliance whose type string contains no solar keyword but declares power_type='solar' must get the solar model.
close_reason: 1db4952: appliance records can declare power_type explicitly; sniff kept as INFO-logged fallback; all 96 packaged fridge rows declared

title: Add CI: run both test suites, the FHIR PoC, and the SUSHI compile on push/PR
description:
There is no .github/ directory at all. 546 tests (177 Python + 369 JS) plus the FHIR transform acceptance checks and the SUSHI FSH compile exist and pass, but nothing runs them on push or PR. For a repo inviting outside contribution this is the single highest-leverage gap: a contributor has no signal their change is sound, and a maintainer has no gate.

  python3 -m pytest tests/ -q                        # 177 tests, needs pydantic/dateutil/pytz

  python3 fhir/transform/run_phase2_poc.py           # 4 acceptance checks; needs fhir.resources (optional dep)

title: HOLD is emitted in seconds-since-power-loss, but schema requires holdover-autonomy in DAYS (values ~86400x too high, schema-invalid)
description:
The simulator's HOLD field is wrong in two compounding ways, both provable against the canonical interop schema cce-interop-0.8.0.json (PQS-DS01-objects/HOLD): title 'Holdover autonomy or independence time', description 'estimated time in days during which all points in the vaccine compartment remain between +2C and +8C if supply power disconnected', minimum 0, maximum 999.9, precision tenths (examples 7.3; worked EMS example reports HOLD ~4.5/4.6 on every record).

ISSUE 1 - WRONG UNIT (seconds vs days, ~86400x scale error). utils/simulator/events.py:329 computes hold = round((timestamp - self._last_power_loss).total_seconds(), 1) -- i.e. SECONDS. The schema unit is DAYS. A simulator value of 4500 is read as 4500 days. It also exceeds the schema maximum of 999.9 after only ~1000s (~17 min) of power loss, so every value past the first sample is schema-INVALID, not merely large. (Tenths rounding is the right precision applied to the wrong unit.)

ISSUE 2 - WRONG SEMANTICS (autonomy rating vs elapsed-since-outage counter). HOLD denotes holdover AUTONOMY: the estimated number of days the vaccine compartment would stay in +2-8C if power were cut -- a near-constant capability of the appliance/thermal reserve, reported CONTINUOUSLY. The schema example shows HOLD ~4.5-4.6 on every record while power is PRESENT (SVA=900, CMPR=0). The simulator instead leaves HOLD null whenever (solar) power is available and then ramps a 'now - last_power_loss' stopwatch (0, 900, 1800, ...). That is a different quantity than the field denotes. Compounds with the solar-nightfall misclassification (is_power_available tied to instantaneous DCSV >= min_operating_voltage in power.py:188-191), so every normal nightfall starts the bogus stopwatch.

REPRO: generate a solar (SDD) device payload; daytime records have HOLD=null, then from the first sample after solar voltage drops HOLD ratchets 0->900->1800->2700->3600->4500 (seconds), climbing one sample-interval per record toward tens of thousands by pre-dawn.
design: Schema (authoritative): cce-interop-0.8.0.json $defs/PQS-DS01-objects/HOLD -> number|null, DAYS, 0..999.9, tenths. HOLD is a holdover-autonomy estimate, reported continuously, near-steady, that DECLINES as thermal/icebank reserve depletes -- NOT a power-outage stopwatch. Proposed fix: derive HOLD (in days) from remaining icebank/thermal reserve (and ambient load), emit it during normal operation (not just outages), bound it <= 999.9, round to tenths. Decouple it from is_power_available so routine solar nightfall does not drive it. Apply the same fix to the JS port to keep parity.
acceptance_criteria: Generated HOLD is in DAYS within [0, 999.9] at tenths precision; present during normal operation (not only during outages) and roughly steady/declining with reserve rather than a linear seconds counter; a generated solar EMS transmission passes ems-record validation with no HOLD range/type finding; Python and JS ports produce equivalent HOLD.
notes: Code sites: Python utils/simulator/events.py:326-329 (hold = total_seconds since _last_power_loss; docstring at :271/:281 says 'seconds since power loss'). JS mirror js/src/events.js:390-395 (comment 'HOLD: seconds since power loss (holdover time)', hold = Math.round((timestamp - _lastPowerLoss)/1000, ...)). Power-availability driver: utils/simulator/power.py:188-191 (solar is_power_available = dcsv >= min_operating_voltage). Related: see the HOLD nightfall-misclassification discussion; this bug supersedes the unit half of that. Acceptance below.
close_reason: HOLD now emitted in DAYS as icebank-reserve holdover autonomy (bounded 0..999.9, tenths), reported continuously by the thermal model; removed from the alarm-layer seconds stopwatch. Python+JS parity, tests + fixtures updated.

title: meta.transferredAt serializes with +00:00 offset instead of trailing Z (rejected 422)
description: utils/schemas.py:20 TransferMetadata.transferredAt is a plain dt.datetime with NO custom serializer. Pydantic model_dump(mode='json') (used in locustfile.py post_packet) emits '2026-03-31T22:58:10.123456+00:00'. The cce-interop-0.8.0 transmission-metadata schema requires meta.transferredAt to match pattern ^2[0-9]{3}-[01][0-9]-[0-3][0-9]T[0-2][0-9]:[0-5][0-9]:[0-5][0-9](\.[0-9]+)?Z$ — i.e. a trailing 'Z', not a numeric offset. Result: every transmission's meta is rejected 422. The emsDateTime serializer used for ABST is fine; transferredAt simply doesn't use a Z-suffix serializer. PYTHON-ONLY: the JS port's TransferMetadata.toJSON() uses Date.toISOString() which already yields '...Z' and is compliant.
acceptance_criteria: meta.transferredAt is emitted as an ISO-8601 UTC string ending in 'Z' (e.g. 2026-03-31T22:58:10Z or with fractional seconds), matching the schema pattern; a generated transmission passes the meta.transferredAt check.
close_reason: Added zuluDateTime PlainSerializer to TransferMetadata.transferredAt; emits ISO-8601 UTC with trailing 'Z' (normalizing any offset to UTC) matching the cce-interop transmission-metadata pattern. Added regression test. JS port already compliant via toISOString().

title: meta.transferType is never emitted (required by schema; absence misroutes RTMD as EMS)
description:
The CCE-interop schema requires meta.transferType with enum [rtm, ems], and uses it in an if/then/else to pick the per-report schema (then=ems-report, else=rtmd-report). utils/schemas.py:TransferMetadata has NO transferType field, and utils/generator.py:transfer_metadata() never sets one, so it is always absent.

Two consequences: (1) 422 'must have required property transferType' on meta; (2) because the schema's 'if' checks meta.transferType against ^ems$, an ABSENT transferType makes the 'if' pass vacuously, so RTMD transmissions get validated against the EMS report schema -> cascade of misleading errors (missing SVA/DCSV/DCCD/BLOG/CMPR/DORV/LERR/LSV...).

FIX: add transferType to TransferMetadata and set it in transfer_metadata() ('ems' for EMS devices, 'rtm' for RTMD).
acceptance_criteria: Generated EMS transmissions carry meta.transferType='ems' and RTMD carry meta.transferType='rtm'; the validator routes each to the correct report schema with no transferType error.
notes: Bug is mirrored in the JS port (same envelope layer). transferType is entirely absent from js/src: transferMetadata() (js/src/device.js:28-36) emits no transferType key, and TransferMetadata (js/src/schemas.js:56-92) neither accepts it in the constructor nor emits it in toJSON(). Fix must add transferType to the JS TransferMetadata + transferMetadata() ('ems' for EMS, 'rtm' for RTMD), matching the Python fix. Core gen untouched.
close_reason: Added meta.transferType (rtm/ems) and changed schemaVersion to semver 0.8.0 in both Python (utils/generator.py, utils/schemas.py) and JS (js/src/device.js, js/src/schemas.js) envelope layers; updated tests. All suites green (153 py, 357 js).

title: schemaVersion 'rtm:1.0'/'ems:1.0' is not a recognized schema version (transmissions rejected 422)
description:
utils/generator.py:transfer_metadata() and utils/schemas.py:TransferMetadata default meta.schemaVersion to 'rtm:1.0' (rtmd) or 'ems:1.0' (ems). The CCE-interop validator treats schemaVersion as an opaque lookup key, normalizes to MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, and exact-matches against vendored schema versions (currently only 0.8.0). 'rtm:1.0'/'ems:1.0' yield no MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH match, so EVERY transmission is rejected 422 'unsupported schemaVersion'. This is the FIRST blocker a supplier hits.

REPRO: generate any report via locustfile/BaseRtmDevice, POST to a validator /i/<uuid> -> 422 with finding 'unsupported schemaVersion "rtm:1.0"; supported: 0.8.0'.

FIX: emit a semver that references the interop schema version the data targets (e.g. '0.8.0'), not a per-device-type label. The transferType (rtm vs ems) should live in meta.transferType (see separate issue), not be encoded into schemaVersion.
acceptance_criteria: meta.schemaVersion is a MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH semver (or full $id URL) matching a validator-supported interop schema version; a generated transmission passes the validator schema-version check (no 'unsupported schemaVersion' finding).
notes: Bug is mirrored in the JS port (same envelope layer). JS sites: js/src/device.js:33 (transferMetadata emits 'rtm:1.0'/'ems:1.0'); js/src/schemas.js:69,75,86 (TransferMetadata defaults schemaVersion='rtm:1.0' and serializes it). Fix must change JS to a real MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH semver too. JS tests assert the buggy values and will need updating: device.test.js:260 ('rtm:1.0'), device.test.js:267 ('ems:1.0'), schemas.test.js:51 ('rtm:1.0'). Core gen (recordset/thermal/power) untouched.
close_reason: Added meta.transferType (rtm/ems) and changed schemaVersion to semver 0.8.0 in both Python (utils/generator.py, utils/schemas.py) and JS (js/src/device.js, js/src/schemas.js) envelope layers; updated tests. All suites green (153 py, 357 js).

title: NEXT BITE: Catalogs loader for JSON and CSV catalog files
description:
## Underlying issues

- ccesim-q25.1: Add a Catalogs loader (ccesim/catalogs.py) — JSON + CSV, normalized key names, loud validation, keep module-level `facilities`/`fridges`/`rtmds`/`dtrs` working.
- ccesim-l58: Treat a blank `power_type` as absent (not invalid) once the CSV path exists.

Read both with `bd show` in full — q25.1's description is the canonical spec (constructors, minimum required fields, key normalization) and is NOT duplicated here.

## Read first

- `bd show ccesim-q25` — the epic body carries verified facts about how the catalogs are consumed (three call sites, only 4 of 21 Facility attributes ever read, js/fixtures independence). Do not re-derive them.
- `bd memories interop` — where the cce-interop requirements/schemas live, if any field naming question comes up.
- `ccesim/facilities.py` — `Facility` dataclass (line 8), `random_facility()` (line 43), the `facilities` list (line 52).
- `ccesim/devicegroups.py` — `Device` dataclass + `from_dict`, `POWER_TYPES`/`validate_power_type()`/`device_label()` (added by q25.3), `DeviceGroup.__init__` and `_resolve_manufacturer_key` (line 226).
- `ccesim/device.py:57,61,65` — the three catalog consumption sites, and `_resolve_power_type` (~line 96).

## Recently-decided context

Landed in commit `1db4952` (ccesim-q25.3, closed) — the loader must build on this, not around it:

- `Device` now has an optional `power_type` field ('solar' | 'mains'). Explicit wins; absent falls back to the type-string sniff, which logs at INFO when it is what decided.
- `ccesim/devicegroups.py` gained module-level helpers the loader should **reuse rather than reimplement**: `POWER_TYPES`, `validate_power_type()`, `device_label()`. Validation currently fires in three places: `Device.from_dict`, `DeviceGroup.__init__` (whole-catalog scan up front, so a bad row fails at load not on the random draw), and `_resolve_power_type` on read.
- Explicit `power_type` values are normalized case/whitespace-insensitively; anything else raises naming the appliance.
- All 96 packaged `fridges` rows now declare `power_type` explicitly. `tests/test_power_type.py:185-194` pins the set of rows whose declared value disagrees with the old sniff to exactly `{E003/124}`, and asserts no packaged appliance takes the sniff path. **If the loader changes how packaged catalogs are constructed, that test must still pass** — treat it as the regression guard for this bite.
- The one deliberate behavior change in the packaged catalog was E003/124 (B Medical `TCW120SDD`) mains → solar. Confirmed correct on review (`E003/123` is the `TCW120AC` sibling). Do not revisit.
- **ccesim-l58 must be handled inside this bite, not after it**: `validate_power_type()` treats `None` as absent but `''` as invalid, and `csv.DictReader` yields `''` for blank cells — so a partially-filled `power_type` column in a user CSV would hard-fail. Blank/whitespace-only must mean absent (fall back to the sniff). Add a test with a CSV whose `power_type` column is filled on some rows and blank on others.

## Slicing recommendation

**One implementer, serial.** The work is a single new module plus edits to two files that all interlock (`catalogs.py` must land with the `devicegroups.py`/`facilities.py` compatibility shims or the module-level names break mid-bite). Splitting would create a shared-file conflict on `devicegroups.py` for no wall-clock gain.

If the implementer wants an internal order:

1. `ccesim/catalogs.py` — `Catalogs` object + the four constructors, key normalization (PQS-style `APQS`/`AMFR`/`AMOD`, `LPQS`/`LMFR`/`LMOD`, NHFR-style facility keys, plus plain equivalents), JSON + CSV readers, loud per-file/per-row validation of the minimum required fields.
2. Fold in ccesim-l58 (blank == absent) while the CSV reader is being written.
3. Retire `DeviceGroup._resolve_manufacturer_key` (devicegroups.py:226) now that normalization happens at load — but keep `DeviceGroup` working when handed raw dicts, since q25.2 has not wired anything yet.
4. Keep `facilities`, `fridges`, `rtmds`, `dtrs` importable at module level with unchanged values — existing code imports them directly and `ccesim-q25.4` (not this bite) is what shrinks them.

Acceptance: `pipenv run pytest tests/ -q` green including the existing `tests/test_power_type.py` guards; a JSON dir and a CSV dir both load; a missing `latitude` errors at load naming file and row; PQS-keyed and plain-keyed inputs both load; extra/unknown columns ride along untouched.

## Out of scope

- **ccesim-q25.2** — do NOT wire `MonitoringDeviceConfig` to accept catalogs, and do NOT add `CCESIM_CATALOG_DIR`. This bite builds the loader; the next one wires it.
- **ccesim-q25.4** — do NOT shrink or re-partition the default catalogs. `Catalogs.builtin(<name>)` may exist as a constructor, but the only builtin it needs to resolve is the current full default set.
- **ccesim-q25.5 / q25.6** — no provenance manifest, no docs, no JS-side reading of the files.
- **ccesim-45r** — catalog provenance/licensing is deliberately parked.
- `js/` and `js/fixtures/` — untouched. `generate_fixtures.py` builds configs directly and does not depend on the catalogs.

## Commit + test expectations

- Verify with `pipenv run pytest tests/ -q` and confirm green before committing. Do not commit unverified work.
- Commit to this repo; do NOT push (the manager session handles landing).
- Commit style: terse sentence-case imperative subject, no bd-id prefix — check `git log --oneline` first.
- One commit is fine if the diff reads cleanly; split q25.1 and the l58 blank-handling only if that genuinely aids review.

title: Shrink the default catalogs to a labelled sample; ship the full sets as named builtins
description:
Once catalogs are pluggable, the packaged ones should read as 'an example, bring your own' rather than as an endorsed reference dataset. Today they are 46 real Sokoto facilities and the full 96/13/7 PQS catalogue, which reads like the latter.

DEFAULT: six to eight facilities spanning a genuine latitude range -- equatorial, tropical, subtropical -- plus about six appliances covering the archetypes the physics actually distinguishes (mains ice-lined, SDD solar, freezer) and two or three loggers. Note this IMPROVES the default demo: all 46 current facilities sit in one Nigerian state, so every simulated fridge today shares one climate.

FULL SETS become named builtins, opt-in:
  Catalogs.builtin('nigeria-sokoto')     # the 46 NHFR/GRID3 facilities
  Catalogs.builtin('pqs-e003-full')      # the full prequalified equipment catalogue

Real or synthetic facilities are both fine, but site them at plausible cold-chain latitudes. Latitude is a physics input, not a label -- it feeds default_config(latitude=...), which drives the ambient temperature cycle and the solar bell curve, so an implausible location produces incoherent output and makes the default-config examples in the README print nonsense.

SAFE TO DO: js/fixtures/ does not depend on the catalogs (generate_fixtures.py uses a fixed LATITUDE = 12.0), so cross-validation cannot break. Check README_JAVASCRIPT.md ('40+ Nigerian facilities') and the README_PYTHON.md structure tree ('Facility data (Sokoto State, Nigeria)') for counts that go stale.

Also drop or wire up ccesim/devicegroups.py 'dtrs' -- 7 records consumed by nothing.

title: Add a Catalogs loader: JSON and CSV, with normalized key names
description:
The foundation. A new ccesim/catalogs.py holding a Catalogs object that carries three lists -- facilities, appliances, loggers -- and knows how to build itself from files.

CONSTRUCTORS:
  Catalogs(facilities=..., appliances=..., loggers=...)     # objects/dicts in hand
  Catalogs.from_dir('./ke-catalog')                          # facilities.json, appliances.json, loggers.json
  Catalogs.from_files(facilities='hfr_export.csv', appliances='our_fridges.json')
  Catalogs.builtin('nigeria-sokoto')                         # named packaged catalog, see the shrink issue

SUPPORT BOTH JSON AND CSV. JSON matches the existing dict shape and the JS port. CSV is what a country program actually has, because the facility list comes out of their HFR or OpenLMIS as a spreadsheet -- csv.DictReader makes this about ten lines. Do not make people convert.

NORMALIZE KEYS ON LOAD. Accept the PQS-style keys (APQS/AMFR/AMOD and LPQS/LMFR/LMOD) so an unmodified E003 or E006 export drops straight in, AND plain pqs_code/manufacturer/model so a country's own list does not have to learn WHO's field names. Same for facilities: accept the NHFR-style keys already in ccesim/facilities.py plus plain equivalents.

This retires DeviceGroup._resolve_manufacturer_key (ccesim/devicegroups.py), which currently sniffs "'AMFR' in self.devices[0]" -- fragile the moment it is handed a mixed or differently-keyed list.

MINIMUM REQUIRED FIELDS (everything else optional, and extras should ride along untouched so users can keep their own join keys):
• Facility: iso, latitude, longitude. Optional but wanted: facility_name.
• Appliance: pqs_code, manufacturer, model, type. Plus the explicit power_type from the sibling issue.
• Logger: pqs_code, manufacturer, model, type.

VALIDATE AND FAIL LOUDLY. A missing latitude must be an error at load, not a None that reaches the thermal model and produces silent nonsense. State which file and which row.

Keep the module-level facilities/fridges/rtmds/dtrs names working -- they are the current public surface and existing code imports them directly.

title: Wire MonitoringDeviceConfig to accept catalogs, plus CCESIM_CATALOG_DIR
description:
Make the loader from the sibling issue actually reachable, at all three levels of ceremony.

1. LIBRARY USE -- pass the object:
   config = MonitoringDeviceConfig(type='ems', catalogs=cat)
   Today MonitoringDeviceConfig takes facility= (a single Facility, device.py:23) and manufacturer=. Add catalogs=; keep facility= working, since passing one specific facility is a distinct and useful thing.

2. FILE USE -- covered by Catalogs.from_dir/from_files.

3. ZERO-CODE USE -- environment variable:
   CCESIM_CATALOG_DIR=./ke-catalog python3 -m locust -f locustfile.py
   This is what makes it a genuine drop-in: it works for locustfile.py, the notebook and any downstream script without touching code.

RESOLUTION ORDER: explicit catalogs= argument > CCESIM_CATALOG_DIR > packaged default. Resolve once and cache; do not re-read files per device, because load testing constructs many devices.

THE ONLY CODE THAT CHANGES is ccesim/device.py:57, 61, 65 -- self.facility = random_facility(), DeviceGroup(fridges), DeviceGroup(rtmds). That is the entire coupling.

Add tests for the precedence chain specifically, including that the env var is ignored when catalogs= is passed.

title: [epic] Pluggable facility and equipment catalogs
description:
FEATURE, not cleanup. Let users of the simulator drop in their own facility list and their own appliance/logger catalogs, overriding the packaged defaults. A country brings its real facility registry and the equipment actually deployed there; a manufacturer brings its own product line. Today both catalogs are hardcoded Python literals and the only way to change them is to edit the package.

WHY THIS IS CHEAP (verified 2026-07-28, do not re-derive):

• The catalogs are consumed in exactly three lines, all in MonitoringDeviceConfig.__init__:
  ccesim/device.py:57  self.facility = random_facility()
  ccesim/device.py:61  dg_f = DeviceGroup(fridges)
  ccesim/device.py:65  dg   = DeviceGroup(rtmds)
• Of the 21 attributes on Facility, FOUR are ever read: iso -> CID, latitude/longitude -> LAT/LNG and the ambient/solar model (device.py:104,141-143,224), and facility_name in a __repr__. nhfr_uid, lga, ward, ownership_type, facility_level_option and a dozen others are inert. So the required schema for a drop-in catalog is tiny.
• js/fixtures/ does NOT depend on the catalogs -- generate_fixtures.py builds configs directly with a fixed LATITUDE = 12.0. Changing or shrinking the defaults cannot break the JS cross-validation fixtures.
• ccesim/devicegroups.py 'dtrs' (7 records) is defined and consumed by nothing.

SHAPE OF THE FEATURE: a Catalogs object with three ways in, resolution order = explicit argument > CCESIM_CATALOG_DIR env var > packaged default. See children for the split.

RELATED: ccesim-45r (catalog provenance/attribution) is deliberately left as-is. Per Benson 2026-07-28: GRID3 and PQS E003/E006 are both public so there is no licensing blocker, and the value of attribution work drops sharply once this epic lands and the shipped defaults shrink. Revisit 45r after.

title: Add a schema-conformance CI job once cce-interop 0.8.1 is published
description:
The CI added in ccesim-33o runs both test suites, the FHIR PoC and the SUSHI compile, but nothing checks that generated output actually validates against the cce-interop schema it claims to emit.

Both implementations hardcode schemaVersion 0.8.1 (utils/generator.py:27, utils/schemas.py:34, js/src/device.js:51, js/src/schemas.js:75) and no copy of the schema is vendored in this repo -- 'find . -name "*schema*.json"' returns nothing.

BLOCKED ON: 0.8.1 being published. It is pending/imminent at https://docs.2to8.cc/cce-data-interop/json-schemas/ ; the file should land at https://schemas.2to8.cc/schemas/cce-interop-0.8.1.json. The authoring location is ../WHO_PQS_E006_EMS_specifications/data_delivery/schemas/, a sibling repo that will NOT be present in CI.

WHEN UNBLOCKED:
1. Decide fetch-at-CI-time vs vendor a pinned copy. Vendoring is more reproducible and makes the repo self-contained for offline contributors; fetching guarantees freshness. The workspace CLAUDE.md documents real drift between authoring folder and published site, so if vendoring, record the source URL and retrieval date next to the file.
2. Add a job that generates one EMS and one RTMD transmission and validates each against ems-report / rtmd-report / transmission-metadata.
3. Do it for BOTH implementations -- the JS port emits the same wire format and is the one most likely to drift.

This closes the loop on the simulator's core claim: that its output is conformant.

title: Make the Python side installable: add pyproject.toml and rename the top-level utils package
description:
There is no pyproject.toml, setup.py, setup.cfg, or requirements.txt. The Python implementation cannot be pip-installed; the only way to use it is to clone and run from the repo root. Two consequences:

1. NOT INSTALLABLE. Anyone wanting the simulator as a library in their own project must vendor it or hack sys.path. The README quickstart works only from the repo root.
2. GENERIC TOP-LEVEL PACKAGE NAME. Imports are 'from utils.simulator import ...' and 'from utils.device import ...'. A top-level package literally called 'utils' will collide with anything else on the path the moment it IS installed. This must be renamed BEFORE publishing to PyPI, not after -- renaming later is a breaking change for every consumer.

BLAST RADIUS OF A RENAME (measure before starting):
- utils/ itself (8 modules incl. utils/simulator/)
- tests/ -- all 9 test modules import from utils
- locustfile.py, js/fixtures/generate_fixtures.py, simulator_examples.ipynb
- fhir/transform/*.py
- README.md, README_PYTHON.md quickstart snippets (both were executed and verified as of c7b8aad -- re-verify after any rename)

SUGGESTED NAME: something specific like ccesim or cce_simulator. Note the JS package is already named 'ems-data-simulator' in js/package.json, so consider whether the two should align.

ALSO: decide whether the Pipfile stays as the source of truth or pyproject.toml takes over. Pipfile was corrected in c7b8aad ([packages] was empty; pydantic, a runtime dep, sat in [dev-packages]) and Pipfile.lock regenerated -- do not undo that split when migrating. Runtime deps: pydantic 2.x, python-dateutil, pytz, tzdata. Everything else is dev.
notes: DECISIONS (2026-07-28, Benson, via /ask): package name = ccesim (matches the bd prefix; free on PyPI, as are cce-simulator and ems-data-simulator). Packaging = pyproject.toml owns metadata + runtime deps; Pipfile keeps the dev environment and installs the project editable, so there is one source of truth for runtime deps and Pipfile.lock still keeps CI deterministic.
close_reason: Landed in e77adfb; CI run on that commit fully green. Package renamed utils -> ccesim across 26 files; pyproject.toml added with setuptools backend, ccesim 0.1.0, requires-python >=3.12. Pipfile [packages] is now just the editable self-install so runtime deps live only in pyproject; [dev-packages] unchanged. Side effect worth knowing: dropping the exact Pipfile pins for pyproject ranges re-resolved runtime deps (pydantic 2.4.2 -> 2.13.4 and friends); 177 tests pass on the new set and js/fixtures regenerated byte-identical, so no behaviour changed. Not published to PyPI; both READMEs say install from source.

title: Add community health files: CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG, code of conduct, security, citation
description:
None of CONTRIBUTING.md, CHANGELOG.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, SECURITY.md or CITATION.cff exist. For a project being handed to the global health community, these are the difference between 'published' and 'open to contribution'.

CONTRIBUTING.md is the one that matters most, and it is not boilerplate here -- the repo has genuinely non-obvious conventions a newcomer will get wrong:
- TWO implementations that must stay behaviourally equivalent. Change the Python physics and the JS port must follow, verified by js/src/cross-validation.test.js against fixtures in js/fixtures/.
- Regenerating fixtures is a Python script run from the repo root: python3 js/fixtures/generate_fixtures.py
- Naming split: Python API snake_case; JS API camelCase; but config FIELD names stay snake_case in BOTH so fixtures need no translation. This trips people.
- Issue tracking is beads (bd), not GitHub Issues, and .beads/issues.jsonl is committed. Contributors need to know whether to file in GitHub or bd -- DECIDE THIS FIRST, it determines what CONTRIBUTING says.
- Do not put bead IDs in source or docs (they were all removed in 03d7be9).
- Internal-only material goes in docs/internal/ (gitignored).
- Test commands: python3 -m pytest tests/ -q and cd js && npm test.

CITATION.cff matters for this audience specifically: researchers using simulated CCE data in papers need something to cite.

CHANGELOG should start at the current state; the schema version bump 0.8.0 -> 0.8.1 (c7b8aad) and the breaking JS camelCase rename (4d52903) are both worth an entry, since the latter breaks existing JS consumers.

title: Document provenance and licensing of the facility and equipment catalogs
description:
utils/facilities.py and utils/devicegroups.py ship real third-party reference data with no attribution, no licence note, and no explanation of why real records are used in a synthetic-data tool. For a global health audience -- the very community these registries belong to -- unattributed use of their own data is a credibility problem, and possibly a licensing one.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY IN THE REPO:
- utils/facilities.py: 46 real facilities, ALL in Sokoto State, Nigeria. Each record carries a real facility name, nhfr_uid, nhfr_facility_code (e.g. '33/17/1/2/1/0001'), exact coordinates, ownership and facility level. Source tags in the data itself: facility_name_source 'NHFR_2024' (Nigeria Health Facility Registry) and geocoordinates_source 'GRID3_EHEALTH'.
- utils/devicegroups.py: 96 fridges, 13 RTMDs, 7 DTRs -- the WHO PQS E003 prequalified equipment catalogue, with real manufacturer and model names (Haier, Vestfrost, B Medical, Dulas, Zero Appliances...).

WHAT ACTUALLY REACHES THE WIRE (verified, do not re-derive):
- Reports emit only CID (country ISO), and LAT/LNG taken from Facility.get_nudged_coordinates() -- utils/device.py:224, 245-246.
- The nudge is random.gauss(0.00001, 0.001) degrees, i.e. ~111 m at 1 sigma. Small: it blurs the exact point but does NOT anonymise the facility.
- Facility NAME, nhfr_uid, and facility code are NOT emitted. They exist only in the source file.

SO THE ISSUE IS THE REPO CONTENT, NOT THE OUTPUT. Both NHFR and GRID3 are public datasets, so this is likely fine legally -- but it needs to be stated, not assumed.

TO DO:
1. Attribute both datasets (source, vintage, licence/terms, link) in README.md and in a header comment in each module.
2. Say why real facilities are used at all (realistic geographic clustering and naming) and document the ~111 m nudge as a deliberate measure, so nobody removes it as noise.
3. Confirm NHFR and GRID3 terms permit redistribution; if not, synthesise the catalogue instead.
4. Consider whether 46 Sokoto-only facilities should be broadened or clearly labelled as a sample -- README_JAVASCRIPT.md already says '40+ Nigerian facilities'.

RELATED CLEANUP: utils/device.py:142-143 set self.lat/self.lng to the RAW un-nudged coordinates, and nothing reads them. Dead attributes that invite a future maintainer to emit un-nudged values by mistake. Remove or rename them.

title: Decision: model ALRM/EERR/LERR as Observation vs DetectedIssue/Flag
description: The one genuine semantic modeling decision. EMS alarms are excursion-timer episodes spanning many records (e.g. HEAT = TVC>8C continuously for 10h), so a single logical alarm covers many intervals. Options: (a) uniform Observation with coded value — easy to query alongside temps, high fidelity per-record; (b) DetectedIssue/Flag per episode — better for alerting/dedup, semantically 'a problem'. Leaning: DetectedIssue per episode (derived in interop layer) WHILE retaining raw per-record ALRM as Observation. Decide with a country/eLMIS consumer in the loop.
design: DECISION (see fhir/decisions/0001-alarm-modeling.md): dual representation by purpose. (1) Per-record ALRM/EERR/LERR codes -> coded Observation (lossless base; Phase 2 already does this). (2) E003 alarm CONDITIONS (HEAT/FRZE/DOOR/POWR) -> ALSO derive one DetectedIssue per contiguous episode in the interop layer (identifiedPeriod, code from PqsE003Alarms, severity HEAT/FRZE=high DOOR/POWR=moderate, implicated->appliance Device). (3) EERR/LERR -> Observation only for now (device-health, not vaccine-safety; promote to DetectedIssue later if actionable). Flag REJECTED (it's a prospective clinician warning, not a detected event). DetectedIssue is DERIVED not transmitted (suppliers still send raw ALRM). Validated: prototype fhir/transform/alarm_episodes.py turns the example 65-record HEAT excursion into 1 DetectedIssue, validates against FHIR R4 (4.0.1) 0 errors. Tests: tests/test_alarm_episodes.py.
close_reason: Decided: dual representation (coded Observation lossless base + derived DetectedIssue per E003 alarm episode; EERR/LERR Observation-only; Flag rejected). Recorded in ADR fhir/decisions/0001-alarm-modeling.md; prototype alarm_episodes.py validates R4 (0 errors), 65 records -> 1 DetectedIssue. Phase 3 (ccesim-jby.5) now unblocked re: alarms; severity taxonomy + evidence links to confirm with consumer there.

title: Locust: include charset in Content-Type header (default utf-8, CHARSET override)
description:
CCE data delivery spec §1.1/§1.2 requires CCE data to be UTF-8-encoded JSON and that the supplier specify content type AND character encoding via the Content-Type header (e.g. 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8'). The Locust module currently relies on the requests json= kwarg, which sets 'application/json' WITHOUT a charset parameter.

Set Content-Type explicitly to 'application/json; charset=<charset>' where charset defaults to 'utf-8' per spec, overridable via a CHARSET env var. This becomes necessary anyway once the gzip issue switches from json= to data= (which drops the auto Content-Type). Coordinate with the gzip issue so Content-Type is set in one place.
acceptance_criteria: POST sends Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8 by default; CHARSET env var overrides the charset parameter value.
close_reason: Implemented and verified in locustfile.py: charset-aware Content-Type (CHARSET, default utf-8), auth via AUTH_HEADER/AUTH_SCHEME/AUTH_TOKEN (covers x-api-key, Bearer, Basic), and optional raw-binary gzip (GZIP) with Content-Encoding: gzip + 1MB §1.4 guard. End-to-end wire test against a mock server confirmed all headers and gzip roundtrip.

title: Locust: support optional gzip request body with Content-Encoding: gzip
description:
The Locust module sends uncompressed JSON (locustfile.py:97 uses the json= kwarg). CCE data delivery spec §1.6 permits (optional, 'may', only if employer supports it) transmitting a raw binary gzip-compressed request body with a Content-Encoding: gzip header. Constraints: body must be RAW binary gzip — shall NOT be further Base64-encoded (no gzip-then-base64). Spec §1.4 also caps request body at 1MB measured AFTER compression (on-the-wire bytes).

Implementation: gate behind a GZIP env var (e.g. GZIP=true). When enabled, switch from json=body to data=gzip.compress(json.dumps(body).encode('utf-8')) and set headers Content-Encoding: gzip plus an explicit Content-Type (see ccesim charset issue). Note: currently one report per POST, so 1MB is unlikely, but consider a post-compression size guard for robustness. Matches validator encoding.ts (§1.6, rejects double-encoding/zip bombs) and size.ts (§1.4 1MB wire cap).
acceptance_criteria: When GZIP is enabled, request body is raw binary gzip (not base64) with Content-Encoding: gzip header; when disabled, behavior is unchanged (plain JSON). Content-Type still set correctly. No double-encoding.
close_reason: Implemented and verified in locustfile.py: charset-aware Content-Type (CHARSET, default utf-8), auth via AUTH_HEADER/AUTH_SCHEME/AUTH_TOKEN (covers x-api-key, Bearer, Basic), and optional raw-binary gzip (GZIP) with Content-Encoding: gzip + 1MB §1.4 guard. End-to-end wire test against a mock server confirmed all headers and gzip roundtrip.

title: Locust: support spec-compliant auth token in configurable HTTP header
description:
The Locust data delivery module (locustfile.py) currently POSTs reports with no authentication (locustfile.py:97, self.client.post(INGEST_PATH, json=body) — no Authorization/token header). CCE data delivery spec §1.3 requires data suppliers to authenticate at the employer's discretion via either (a) an access token in an employer-specified HTTP header (header NAME configurable per country, e.g. x-api-key) or (b) HTTP Basic Auth.

DESIGN — LOCKED ON OPTION B (scheme-prefix generalization). One mechanism subsumes the spec's two methods plus standard Bearer. Three env vars:
- AUTH_HEADER (default 'x-api-key') — header name, configurable per §1.3
- AUTH_SCHEME (default empty/unset) — optional auth scheme prefix (e.g. 'Bearer', 'Basic')
- AUTH_TOKEN — the secret value; when unset, NO auth header is sent (auth disabled)

Build the header value as: f'{AUTH_SCHEME} {AUTH_TOKEN}'.strip() when AUTH_SCHEME is set, else AUTH_TOKEN verbatim. Then headers = {AUTH_HEADER: value}. Pass into client.post.

Covers all three shapes from one path:
- API-key (spec §1.3 default): AUTH_HEADER=x-api-key, AUTH_SCHEME unset, AUTH_TOKEN=<key> -> 'x-api-key: <key>'
- Bearer (superset of spec; for OAuth-protected employer endpoints): AUTH_HEADER=Authorization, AUTH_SCHEME=Bearer, AUTH_TOKEN=<token> -> 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
- Basic (spec §1.3): AUTH_HEADER=Authorization, AUTH_SCHEME=Basic, AUTH_TOKEN=<base64(user:pass)> -> 'Authorization: Basic <b64>'

Token is an opaque secret — do NOT assume/parse JWT. Note: Bearer is NOT named in spec §1.3 (which lists only header-token and Basic) — it is a deliberate superset; the validator (cce-data-delivery-validator/src/ingest/stages/auth.ts) models only 'header' and 'basic'.
acceptance_criteria: When AUTH_TOKEN is set, POST includes the AUTH_HEADER header (default x-api-key) with value = AUTH_SCHEME + ' ' + AUTH_TOKEN when AUTH_SCHEME is set, else AUTH_TOKEN verbatim. When AUTH_TOKEN is unset, no auth header is sent. Verified for all three configs: x-api-key (no scheme), Authorization: Bearer, and Authorization: Basic.
close_reason: Implemented and verified in locustfile.py: charset-aware Content-Type (CHARSET, default utf-8), auth via AUTH_HEADER/AUTH_SCHEME/AUTH_TOKEN (covers x-api-key, Bearer, Basic), and optional raw-binary gzip (GZIP) with Content-Encoding: gzip + 1MB §1.4 guard. End-to-end wire test against a mock server confirmed all headers and gzip roundtrip.

title: JS toJSON() strips null-valued required fields (ALRM, EERR, LERR) — omits schema-required keys (422)
description: js/src/schemas.js EmsRecord.toJSON (lines 128-139) and RtmdRecord.toJSON (231-242) skip any field whose value is undefined OR null ('if (v === undefined || v === null) continue;'). But ems-record REQUIRES ALRM, EERR, LERR (and rtmd-record requires ALRM, EERR), with type ['string','null'] — i.e. the KEY must be present and null is an allowed value. During normal operation ALRM/EERR/LERR are null, so the JS output omits these required keys entirely and the record is schema-invalid (422). Confirmed by running toEms('mains'): output = {ABST,BEMD,BLOG,CMPR,DORV,TAMB,TVC,ACCD,ACSV,SVA} with no ALRM/EERR/LERR. The Python port is correct: model_dump(exclude_unset=True) keeps explicitly-set null fields, emitting 'ALRM':null,'EERR':null,'LERR':null. Parity break in the port. Fix: only strip undefined, not null, for record serialization (or always emit the required keys).
acceptance_criteria: JS EMS/RTMD records always include the schema-required keys (ALRM, EERR, LERR for EMS; ALRM, EERR for RTMD) with explicit null when unset, matching Python output and the schema's required list.
close_reason: Fixed in commits 5285bb9 (m1r) and a5c07d6 (6l0); 364 JS tests pass, production output verified to emit ALRM/EERR/LERR:null and uppercase-Z ABST.

title: ABST serialized with lowercase 'z' in JS port — fails schema ABST regex (requires uppercase Z)
description: js/src/schemas.js:24 formatEmsDateTime() returns the EMS datetime with a trailing lowercase 'z' (e.g. '20240615T000000z'). The cce-interop ABST object is pattern-constrained to '^2[0-9]{7}T[0-2][0-9]{5}(\.[0-9]+)?Z$' (uppercase Z; example '20200115T040554Z'), so every EMS and RTMD record emitted by the JS port is schema-invalid and would be rejected 422. The Python port is correct: utils/schemas.py:11 appends uppercase 'Z'. This is a JS/Python parity break introduced in the port. Fix formatEmsDateTime to emit 'Z'. Verified: js fixtures/mains_normal.json records show 'ABST':'20240615T000000z'.
acceptance_criteria: JS formatEmsDateTime emits a trailing uppercase 'Z'; emitted ABST values match the schema regex and Python output.
close_reason: Fixed in commits 5285bb9 (m1r) and a5c07d6 (6l0); 364 JS tests pass, production output verified to emit ALRM/EERR/LERR:null and uppercase-Z ABST.

title: Eliminate OpenFn references
description: OpenFn is a platform that is used by some countries for CCE data ingestion. To make this tool more generalized, OpenFn references should be eliminated. This includes AT LEAST the OPENFN_WORKFLOW_ID variable for the Locust data delivery configuration . . . which would force us to revisit a more generic way to define the ingestion URL (separating host and workflow ID is probably unnecessary).
close_reason: Replaced OPENFN_WORKFLOW_ID with generic INGEST_PATH in locustfile; updated README + notebook to vendor-neutral language. Committed 8c5e8a0.

title: RTMD reports omit required AMID and DLST fields (rtmd-report rejected 422)
description:
utils/device.py:create_report() builds the RtmdReport object without AMID (Appliance Monitoring ID) or DLST (device/sensor list), and utils/schemas.py:RtmdReport does not model them. The interop schema's rtmd-report REQUIRES both AMID (string) and DLST (object mapping performance properties like TVC/TFRZ/TAMB to sensor definitions {SID,SMFR,SMOD}). Their absence yields 422 'must have required property AMID' and 'DLST'.

FIX: add AMID (a stable appliance-monitoring id, e.g. tenant/facility/equipment ref) and DLST (built from the device's sensor metadata) to RtmdReport and populate them in create_report().
acceptance_criteria: Generated RTMD reports include AMID (string) and a DLST mapping at least TVC to a sensor definition; an RTMD transmission passes rtmd-report validation with no missing AMID/DLST findings.
notes: UNBLOCKED (2026-06-02): authoritative schema now available at ../docs-2to8-cc/docs/cce-data-interop/schemas/cce-interop-0.8.0.json (simulator emits schemaVersion 0.8.0). Read the rtmd-report / AMID / DLST definitions there and implement the EXACT required shape in both the Python reference (utils/schemas.py + utils/device.py) and the JS port. Available metadata to build DLST: device logger fields lser/lmfr/lmod; appliance fields amfr/amod/cid for AMID.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 155d12c. Added AMID + DLST to Python reference and JS port per cce-interop-0.8.0 rtmd-report; AMID stable per device, DLST maps TVC/TAMB to sensor defs. Verified: both ports' RTMD transfers validate against cce-interop-0.8.0.json; 159 Python + 366 JS tests pass.

title: ACCD/DCCD emit power-availability seconds instead of current amps (out of schema range)
description:
utils/simulator/power.py:162 SolarPowerModel.simulate_interval sets 'DCCD': round(powered_s, 1), where powered_s is cumulative SECONDS of DC power availability in the interval (0-900). Per DS01/the interop schema, DCCD is 'DC current drawn by the appliance' in AMPERES with max 99.9. Emitting up to 900 yields 422 'DCCD must be <= 99.9' on every solar EMS record. This looks like a mis-port of the mains SVA (supply-voltage-availability seconds) concept into the solar DC-current field.

FIX: emit a realistic DC current (amps) for DCCD (e.g. derived from compressor load / DC power model), and if availability-seconds is the intended quantity, carry it in an appropriate field rather than DCCD.
acceptance_criteria: Solar EMS records emit DCCD as a DC current in amps within [0, 99.9]; a solar EMS transmission passes validation with no DCCD range finding.
notes: SCOPE BROADENED: this is NOT solar-only. The mains path has the identical bug. utils/simulator/power.py:85 sets 'ACCD': round(powered_s,1) (interval seconds, 0 or 900); schema ACCD is AC current amps with min 0.01, max 49.99 -> 900 fails max when powered, 0 fails min during outage. utils/simulator/power.py:162 sets 'DCCD': round(powered_s,1) likewise; schema DCCD is DC current amps min 0, max 99.9 -> 900 fails max. Both mains-EMS and solar-EMS records are rejected. FIX both ACCD (mains) and DCCD (solar) to emit a modeled current draw in amps within range (and >= 0.01 for ACCD), not the availability-seconds value. NOTE: availability-seconds for mains already belongs in SVA (0-900) — see separate SVA issue.
close_reason: ACCD (mains) and DCCD (solar) now emit a modeled current draw in amps derived from compressor duty cycle, clamped to schema ranges (ACCD [0.01,49.99], DCCD [0,99.9]) instead of availability-seconds (0-900). Added tunable current params to PowerConfig (py+js), fixed both ports, updated unit tests, regenerated cross-validation fixtures (only ACCD/DCCD changed - no RNG desync). 155 py + 358 js pass.

title: to_ems() drops required EERR by popping it into LERR (EMS records rejected 422)
description:
utils/simulator/recordset.py:262-264 in to_ems() does: if 'EERR' in filtered: filtered['LERR'] = filtered.pop('EERR'). This MOVES EERR into LERR, so the emitted EMS record has LERR but no EERR. The interop schema's ems-record requires BOTH EERR and LERR, so every EMS record fails with 'must have required property EERR' -> 422.

FIX: populate LERR and EERR independently (e.g. copy rather than pop, or generate distinct logger vs EMD error codes). EERR (EMD error codes) and LERR (logger error codes) are different DS01 objects and should both be present.
design: Context & proposed resolution: Errors on loggers (LERR) and EMDs (EERR) are defined by manufacturers and are likely highly independent of one another. The reasonable fix is to generate LERR values using the same rng / stochastic mechanism as EERR. They do not need to be coupled — each can be a separate roll of the die. Concretely: in events.py AlarmGenerator.compute (and js/src/events.js), add an independent low-probability LERR draw alongside the existing EERR draw, emit both fields, and in to_ems() copy/populate EERR and LERR independently instead of popping EERR into LERR.
acceptance_criteria: Emitted EMS records include both EERR and LERR; an EMS transmission passes ems-record validation with no missing-EERR finding.
notes: Investigation: EERR is produced ONLY in utils/simulator/events.py:329-332 (AlarmGenerator.compute) as random noise — 0.1% chance per sample (rng.random() < 0.001), value is a random 5-char lowercase string. It is NOT tied to any physical fault (power outage, compressor failure, leak, stuck door drive ALRM/HOLD/temperature, never EERR). JS port mirrors this at js/src/events.js:399-405. LERR is never generated independently anywhere — it only becomes non-null in to_ems() by relabeling the already-random EERR. So today both 'codes' derive from a single EERR draw; the pop additionally strips EERR (the 422).
close_reason: Generate LERR as an independent low-probability draw alongside EERR in AlarmGenerator (Python + JS); to_ems() now carries EERR and LERR through independently instead of popping EERR into LERR. EMS records emit both fields; no more missing-EERR 422. Tests updated, both suites green (py 155, js 358).

title: Treat a blank power_type as absent when the CSV catalog loader lands
description:
Follow-up from the ccesim-q25.3 review (commit 1db4952), for whoever implements ccesim-q25.1 (Catalogs loader: JSON and CSV).

ccesim/devicegroups.py:31-38 validate_power_type() treats None as 'absent' (returns None, caller falls back to the type-string sniff) but treats an empty or whitespace-only string as an INVALID value and raises:

    validate_power_type('', label)
    -> ValueError: Invalid power_type '' for appliance E003/999 (X Y): expected one of 'solar', 'mains'

That is the correct, loud behaviour for a hand-written JSON catalog. It is the wrong behaviour for CSV, which is the other format q25.1 must accept: csv.DictReader yields '' for every blank cell, so a user catalog with a power_type column that is only filled in for the rows they care about will fail to load entirely, with an error that points at a row they intentionally left blank.

Suggested resolution when q25.1 lands: normalize '' / whitespace-only to None inside validate_power_type (i.e. treat blank as 'not stated' and fall through to the sniff), or have the CSV reader drop empty cells before constructing the record. Either way add a test for a CSV row with a blank power_type cell.

Not a defect in 1db4952 - nothing in the shipped catalogs or the JSON path hits it today, and q25.1 was explicitly out of scope for that bite.

title: Document the catalog format, and let the JS port read the same files
description:
The payoff of a documented JSON format: a country writes ONE catalog and it works in both implementations.

Today the JS port has no catalog at all -- README_JAVASCRIPT.md:146 says 'Facility catalog | 40+ Nigerian facilities | Not included -- pass metadata via config'. So JS users hand-build metadata per device. If the Python side gains a documented JSON schema for facilities/appliances/loggers, the JS side can load the same file and the two stop diverging on this.

SCOPE:
1. Document the format properly in README_PYTHON.md and README.md: required vs optional fields, both accepted key spellings (PQS-style and plain), JSON and CSV, and a complete worked example of a small custom catalog.
2. Add a JS loader reading the same JSON. Keep the config-field naming convention the two ports already follow -- Python API snake_case, JS API camelCase, but config FIELD names stay snake_case in BOTH so no translation layer is needed. Catalog files are config, so their field names stay snake_case in JS too.
3. Add a cross-implementation test that both ports load the same catalog file and agree on what they read.

Do this LAST in the epic -- it documents whatever the loader and the shrink issues actually settle on, so writing it earlier means rewriting it.

title: Give each catalog a provenance manifest
description:
Once catalogs are files rather than Python literals, provenance has a natural structural home: a manifest sitting next to each catalog carrying source, vintage, licence, url and retrieved date.

This is better than a comment in a .py because it makes THIRD-PARTY catalogs self-describing too -- a country that shares its facility list ships the terms with it -- and because tooling can read it.

For the packaged catalogs the values are known: facilities are NHFR_2024 (Nigeria Health Facility Registry) for names and GRID3_EHEALTH for coordinates, both already recorded per-record in the data itself; equipment is the WHO PQS E003/E006 prequalified catalogue. Both public.

Also fold in the small cleanup: ccesim/device.py:142-143 set self.lat/self.lng to the RAW un-nudged coordinates and NOTHING reads them (only get_nudged_coordinates() at device.py:224 reaches the wire). Dead attributes that invite a future maintainer to emit un-nudged values by mistake. Remove them.

And document the ~111 m coordinate nudge (facilities.py:36-37, random.gauss(0.00001, 0.001) degrees) as deliberate, so nobody strips it as noise -- and so users supplying their own facility list understand it applies to theirs too.

RELATIONSHIP TO ccesim-45r: 45r is the pre-existing attribution issue against the current hardcoded catalogs and is deliberately being left alone for now. This issue is the version of that work that makes sense AFTER the catalogs are pluggable and the defaults have shrunk. Expect to close one of the two.

title: Seed fhir/transform/run_phase2_poc.py so the CI acceptance checks are deterministic
description:
run_phase2_poc.py is now a CI gate (ccesim-33o) but is unseeded. build_transmission() constructs a MonitoringDeviceConfig with no seed, so the facility and fridge model are drawn at random on every run.

MEASURED VARIANCE (10 consecutive local runs, all PASS): observation counts 7840-8640, coded alarm counts 60-98.

WHY IT MATTERS: the fourth acceptance check asserts 'coded alarm Observations emitted > 0'. It depends on the compressor-failure holdover exhausting inside the 9-day horizon, and holdover depends on the randomly chosen fridge model and ambient climate. The module comment itself notes 'a short run shows no alarm: the holdover hasn't run out yet, not a defect' -- so a long-holdover appliance is exactly the case that would fail the check without anything being wrong. 10/10 passed with comfortable margin, so this is a latent flake, not an active one.

FIX: seed the PoC (fixed facility + fixed fridge model, or an explicit random seed) so the printed counts are reproducible and the gate is honest. Keep the assertion as-is; the point is to remove the draw, not to weaken the check.

Deliberately not done inside ccesim-33o: it changes FHIR PoC behaviour and the printed numbers, which belongs with the FHIR work rather than with wiring up CI.

title: README.md does not mention the FHIR work or the validator relationship
description:
Two things a reader of the top-level README cannot discover:

1. fhir/ is invisible. It is a tracked subproject with logical models, terminology (71 PQS object codes), a StructureMap, an executable reference transformer, an ADR, and a validation harness -- and README.md never mentions it. fhir/README.md was made self-contained in c7b8aad, so all that is needed is a pointer plus one line of framing, and a note that the work is draft/experimental and NOT endorsed by WHO or HL7 (the canonical URLs deliberately use a worldhealthorg.example placeholder pending a namespace-ownership decision). That non-endorsement notice currently lives ONLY in fhir/README.md; a reader who never opens that directory never sees it.

2. The validator relationship is unstated. The simulator's purpose is being the first producer feeding ../cce-data-delivery-validator, and the two evolve together (see the project CLAUDE.md). Nothing public says so, which leaves the 'why does this exist' answer incomplete -- README.md now has a 'Who this is for' section (c7b8aad) that would be the natural home.

Small, purely additive, no code impact.

title: Fill in js/package.json metadata before any npm publish
description:
js/package.json is missing license, repository, author, files, engines and keywords. Present: name 'ems-data-simulator', version 0.1.0, description, main, exports, scripts.test, deps.

The license gap matters most: the repo has an MIT LICENSE file (c) 2026 Phoenix Global Health, but neither ecosystem can read it programmatically -- npm sees no 'license' field and Python has no packaging metadata at all (see the pyproject issue). Tooling that audits dependency licences will report this package as unlicensed.

TO DO: add license 'MIT', repository (git+https://github.com/phoenixgh-org/ems-data-simulator.git with directory 'js'), author, files (whitelist src/ so fixtures and tests are not shipped), engines (Node version -- vitest 4 and the ESM/import syntax used imply a modern floor, check before asserting), keywords.

NOTE: version is still 0.1.0 and the package appears unpublished. The camelCase API rename in 4d52903 was a clean break with no back-compat aliases -- if this is ever published, that history should be reflected in the version chosen.
notes:
DECISION (2026-07-28, Benson): no npm publish is intended. Consumers who want a package can build one locally. That removes the reason for 'files', 'engines' and 'keywords', and removes the versioning question entirely.

What still has value independent of publishing: the 'license' field, so licence-audit tooling reading js/package.json does not report the package as unlicensed, and 'repository' now that the canonical remote is settled. Rescope to those two fields, or close as won't-do.

title: Docs: internal beads IDs remain in test-file comments
description:
~14 references to internal tracker IDs (ccesim-l5u, ccesim-fuq, ccesim-l0s, ccesim-jby.3/.4) remain in comments under tests/ and js/src/*.test.js. They dangle for a public reader the same way the FHIR ones did.

The FHIR set was stripped in c7b8aad; these were left because the agreed scope covered fhir/ only. Low visibility (test comments, not user-facing docs).
close_reason: Closed

title: Decide: js default_config vs camelCase API convention
description:
js/src/config.js:221 exports default_config (snake_case). Every other function in the JS port is camelCase (createReport, toEms, toRtmd, getState). The docs had drifted to defaultConfig and were broken until c7b8aad corrected them to match the code.

Options: (a) leave as-is, (b) add a camelCase defaultConfig alias export for consistency while keeping default_config for back-compat, (c) rename with a deprecation shim.

Config FIELDS are deliberately snake_case to mirror Python (fault_type, random_seed), so the function name is the only inconsistency.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 2 follow-up: execute cce-interop-to-bundle.fml through a real engine (Matchbox/validator) in Java-enabled CI
description: The Phase 2 StructureMap (fhir/input/maps/cce-interop-to-bundle.fml) is the canonical transform but was NOT executed by a real FML engine during ccesim-jby.4 — no JVM was available locally (Matchbox and the HL7 validator -transform are Java-only). The Python reference transformer (fhir/transform/cce_to_fhir.py) proved the mapping end-to-end and its output validates against FHIR R4B via fhir.resources. This task: in a Java-enabled CI, compile the .fml to a StructureMap and run it (Matchbox $transform or validator_cli -transform) over fhir/examples/ems-transmission.json, then assert the engine output matches the reference transformer's Bundle (modulo resource ids). Also: complete the per-object Observation rules in the .fml (currently representative-per-unit-class) by generating them from the UNITS table in cce_to_fhir.py.
acceptance_criteria: FML compiles to a StructureMap; engine transform of the example transmission succeeds and matches cce_to_fhir.py output structurally; CI step wired so the two implementations stay in lockstep.
notes: Java validator (validator_cli.jar v6.9.10, JDK 21) now available locally. Findings: (1) Python-produced Bundle now validates against FHIR R4 PROPER (4.0.1) with 0 errors (warnings best-practice only). Java validator caught 3 real bugs the pure-Python fhir.resources/R4B missed -> fixed in cce_to_fhir.py: urn:uuid fullUrls must be valid UUIDs (->resource-typed URLs); RESTful fullUrl must end /{type}/{id} matching resource.id; coding.display must match CodeSystem exactly (->display omitted). (2) FML transform still NOT executable: (a) GRAMMAR - cannot chain a 'then {}' block with a comma in a target list (Error @ Found ',' expecting ';'); must restructure into separate rules using flat source paths. (b) SHAPE MISMATCH - the .fml reads grouped logical-model paths (report.appliance.AMFR) but cce-interop wire JSON is FLAT (report.AMFR); needs either a flat 'wire' source model or a wire->logical pre-step. Fixing both = core of this issue. Validator invocation: java -jar validator_cli.jar <bundle> -ig fhir/fsh-generated/resources -version 4.0.1; transform: ... <src.json> transform <map-url> -ig <map.fml> -ig fhir/fsh-generated/resources -version 4.0.1 -output <out>. NOTE: FML comments must be // not /// (/// is metadata syntax).

title: Phase 4: Fold FHIR validation into the simulator<->validator conformance loop
description: Extend the existing simulator <-> cce-data-delivery-validator relationship so every cce-interop schema bump is checked against BOTH the JSON schema AND the FHIR profiles. Simulator output (already cce-interop-0.8.0-conformant with realistic faults and Annex-edge values) becomes the canonical FHIR conformance fixtures: generate -> StructureMap -> HL7 FHIR Validator against profiles.
acceptance_criteria: A repeatable conformance suite runs simulator output through the StructureMap and validates against published profiles; failures surface on schema/profile changes.

title: Phase 3: Resource profiles + ConceptMaps + IG packaging (Option B)
description: Profile Observation/Device/Location/Organization per the assessment mapping table; map transmission meta to Bundle+MessageHeader; borrow DeviceMetric for sampling/averaging metadata (e.g. 'average of raw samples at <=10s within each 15-min period') and per-device battery units (BEMD/BLOG % vs V). Author ConceptMaps from PQS codes to LOINC/UCUM where a faithful equivalent exists; local concepts for cold-chain-specific objects (HOLD, SVA, compressor duty cycle) with proposals to LOINC later. Apply the ALRM modeling decision (ccesim-jby.3). Package as an HL7 IG via IG Publisher. Plan for resource explosion (~70k Observations/device/year): grouped Observation.component[] or FHIR-as-query-projection.
acceptance_criteria: Profiles + ConceptMaps published in an IG; Phase 2 Bundle validates against profiles with the HL7 FHIR Validator; RTMD vs EMS handled via transferType-discriminated profiles incl. rtmd-sensor-schema sensor->TVC/TFRZ/TAMB mapping.

title: cce-interop-0.8.0 schema BLOG max 9999.9/decimal contradicts PQS Annex-1 (max 9999, integer days)
description: The cce-interop JSON schema (docs-2to8-cc/docs/cce-data-interop/schemas/cce-interop-0.8.0.json, $defs/PQS-DS01-objects/BLOG) sets BLOG maximum=9999.9 with example 367.4 (1 dp). The authoritative PQS E006 DS01.2 Annex-1 specifies BLOG (Logger battery remaining) Max Value=9999 with Data Format 0000 and Unit DDDD -- i.e. WHOLE DAYS, integer precision. This contrasts with the sibling BEMD (EMD battery remaining), which the Annex defines as Data Format 000.0, Unit DDDD.D, max 9999.9 -- and which the schema matches correctly. The schema appears to have applied BEMD's decimal bound/precision to BLOG. FIX: set BLOG maximum 9999.9 -> 9999 and align the example/precision with integer days (Annex Data Format 0000).
acceptance_criteria: cce-interop-0.8.0.json BLOG maximum is 9999 and its example reflects integer days (matching PQS Annex-1 Data Format 0000), while BEMD remains 9999.9/1dp.
close_reason: Schema BLOG maximum 9999.9 -> 9999 and example -> integer 367; simulator BLOG clamp tightened to 9999 in both ports

title: cce-interop-0.8.0 schema DRCV/DRCF maximum 900 contradicts PQS Annex-1 (no max; count not seconds)
description: The cce-interop JSON schema (docs-2to8-cc/docs/cce-data-interop/schemas/cce-interop-0.8.0.json, $defs/PQS-DS01-objects/DRCV and DRCF) sets maximum=900 for both. DRCV/DRCF are 'Number of door/lid openings within each 15-minute period' (a COUNT, Data Format 000, Unit N/A). The authoritative PQS E006 DS01.2 Annex-1 specifies Max Value=none for both (Data Format 000 implies a 0-999 range). The schema's 900 appears copy-pasted from the sibling DORV/DORF objects, which ARE durations in seconds (max 900 s per 15-min period). Applying a seconds-derived cap to an opening COUNT is semantically wrong and could reject legitimately high counts. FIX: remove the maximum:900 constraint from DRCV and DRCF (or set to 999 to match the 000 format), matching the Annex.
acceptance_criteria: cce-interop-0.8.0.json DRCV and DRCF no longer carry a 900 maximum derived from the seconds-based door-duration objects; bound (if any) reflects the count Data Format 000.
close_reason: Annex is wrong. Cap is matched to EMS 15-minute max window

title: cce-interop-0.8.0 schema ACCD maximum 49.99 contradicts PQS Annex-1 (max 50)
description: The cce-interop JSON schema (docs-2to8-cc/docs/cce-data-interop/schemas/cce-interop-0.8.0.json, $defs/PQS-DS01-objects/ACCD) sets ACCD maximum=49.99, but the authoritative PQS E006 DS01.2 Annex-1 (pqs-e006-ds01.2-annex-1-cold-chain-data-objects.xlsx, Data Objects sheet) specifies ACCD Max Value=50 with Data Format 00.00 (2 dp). The 49.99 ceiling excludes the valid maximum reading 50.00. Companion to ccesim-8yq (which covers the ACCD minimum 0.01 vs 0). FIX: amend schema ACCD maximum 49.99 -> 50 to match the Annex.
acceptance_criteria: cce-interop-0.8.0.json ACCD maximum is 50 (matching PQS Annex-1).
close_reason: Schema ACCD maximum 49.99 -> 50 in cce-interop-0.8.0.json

title: cce-interop-0.8.0 schema ACCD minimum 0.01 contradicts PQS Annex-1 (min 0)
description: The cce-interop JSON schema (docs-2to8-cc/docs/cce-data-interop/schemas/cce-interop-0.8.0.json, $defs/PQS-DS01-objects/ACCD) sets ACCD minimum=0.01, but the authoritative PQS E006 DS01.2 Annex-1 (pqs-e006-ds01.2-annex-1-cold-chain-data-objects.xlsx, Data Objects sheet) specifies ACCD Min Value=0 with Data Format 00.00 (max 50). The 0.01 floor was an over-tightening with no spec basis. As of resolving ccesim-fuq/ccesim-ups the simulator now emits ACCD=0 during mains outage/no-draw per the Annex, which would 422 against the unmodified schema's 0.01 minimum. FIX: amend the schema (and any downstream copies) ACCD minimum 0.01 -> 0 to match the Annex. Lives in the docs-2to8-cc repo, hence tracked separately from the simulator change.
acceptance_criteria: cce-interop-0.8.0.json ACCD minimum is 0 (matching PQS Annex-1); simulator output with ACCD=0 validates against the schema.
close_reason: Schema ACCD minimum 0.01 -> 0 in cce-interop-0.8.0.json; ACCD=0 outage output validates

title: POWER_OUTAGE/PROGRAMMED outage fault leaves SVA=900, ACSV/ACCD at powered values
description: The POWER_OUTAGE fault sets FaultEffects.power_available_override=False (utils/simulator/events.py get_fault_effects), which drives power_available/compressor/alarms in recordset.py. But power_model.simulate_interval() is called independently and keys SVA/ACSV/ACCD off its OWN MainsPowerModel.state.in_outage, which the fault never sets. Result: during a POWER_OUTAGE fault the mains power record still reads SVA=900 (full in-bounds seconds), ACSV~=nominal, ACCD at running current -- i.e. the power telemetry ignores the modeled outage. Confirmed in regenerated js/fixtures/power_outage.json (all 24 records SVA=900). Pre-existing; surfaced while fixing ccesim-60b (SVA seconds) and ccesim-bua (ACCD amps), which only addressed the stochastic-outage path. FIX: thread power_available (or the override) into MainsPowerModel/SolarPowerModel.simulate_interval so SVA->0, ACSV->0, ACCD->floor during any outage (stochastic OR fault). Mirror in JS. Note: skipping the rng.gauss(ACSV) call during a fault outage will shift RNG sequencing -> regenerate cross-validation fixtures. Applies to both ports.
acceptance_criteria: During a POWER_OUTAGE fault, mains EMS records emit SVA=0, ACSV=0, and ACCD at the schema floor (0.01); power_outage fixture shows SVA=0 across the outage window. Both Python and JS.
close_reason: Threaded power_available_override into Mains/SolarPowerModel.simulate_interval (both ports) + recordset. A POWER_OUTAGE fault now forces SVA=0/ACSV=0/ACCD=0 (mains) and DCCD=0/battery-drain (solar) for the interval, not just stochastic outages. Regenerated power_outage fixture (SVA 900->0). Resolved jointly with ccesim-ups.

title: EERR/LERR emit random 5-letter gibberish instead of pre-defined error codes
description: EERR and LERR are generated as five random lowercase letters at low probability (utils/simulator/events.py:331-340; js/src/events.js:399-418, e.g. 'qxzra'). The cce-interop schema describes EERR/LERR as 'Alphanumeric codes corresponding to conditions...' and the PQS Annex (pqs-e006-ds01.2-annex-1, 'Error Codes' sheet + Data Objects format note) defines them as 'pre-defined error codes with 1 to 7 characters; multiple codes space-separated, e.g. "COMM PWR"'. Random gibberish passes the bare JSON-schema string type but is not a recognized code, so downstream consumers can't interpret it and it doesn't reflect real EMD/logger behavior. Draw from the predefined set (Annex compressor codes 0-7, EMD 'COMM', etc.; space-separate when multiple). Applies to both Python and JS.
acceptance_criteria: EERR/LERR values, when present, are drawn from the Annex predefined error-code set (1-7 chars each, space-separated for multiples), not random letters.
close_reason: EERR/LERR now drawn from pre-defined Annex code sets (EMD: compressor codes 1-7 + COMM; Logger: COMM/SENS/BATT/RTC/MEM), 1-7 chars, space-separated for multiples, via _pick_error_codes helper. Replaced 5-random-letter gibberish. Both ports.

title: Mains nominal_voltage default 600 V drives ACSV above schema max (600) — ~48% of records overflow
description: PowerConfig.nominal_voltage defaults to 600 (utils/simulator/config.py:121; js/src/config.js:71). The docstring (config.py:95) even says 'Normal mains voltage (V), maps to SVA field' — 600 V is not a normal mains voltage (real AC mains is ~120-240 V; schema ACSV example is 235.3) and 600 is exactly the schema ACSV maximum. ACSV is then computed as round1(nominal + gauss(0, nominal*0.02)) (power.py:79 / power.js:98), so the Gaussian noise (sigma=12 V) regularly pushes ACSV ABOVE the schema max of 600 -> schema-invalid. Verified over 200 generated mains records (seed 7): 95/200 ACSV values exceed 600, max 635.3. Set a realistic nominal AC voltage (e.g. ~230) so ACSV sits well within [0,600]. Applies to both Python and JS. Related to but distinct from the SVA value mix-up (ccesim-60b).
acceptance_criteria: Default mains supply voltage is realistic (~230 V) and emitted ACSV stays within the schema range [0,600] across normal generation; no records exceed 600.
close_reason: Default mains nominal_voltage 600->230 V (py config.py, js config.js); ACSV now derived from realistic 230 V nominal. Verified 0/500 mains records exceed schema max 600 (range 215.5-241.5). Docstring corrected (maps to ACSV, not SVA).

title: BLOG/BEMD emit battery voltage instead of days of battery life remaining
description: Schema defines BLOG ('Logger battery remaining') and BEMD ('EMD battery remaining') as estimated DAYS of battery life remaining (min 0, max 9999.9; examples 367.4, 14.3). The simulator emits a battery VOLTAGE (~11-14): solar at utils/simulator/power.py:163-164 (blog_voltage_empty + soc*range) and mains at utils/simulator/recordset.py:197-200 (round(gauss(12.0,0.3))). Both land in 0-9999.9 so no 422, but the modeled quantity is wrong (volts where days are expected). Decide on a realistic days-remaining model for BLOG and BEMD. Applies to both Python and JS ports (mirror the fix).
acceptance_criteria: BLOG and BEMD represent estimated days of battery life remaining (plausible day-scale values), not a battery voltage.
close_reason: BLOG/BEMD now estimated DAYS of battery life remaining (schema [0,9999.9]): solar scales from logger SOC * blog_full_days/bemd_full_days (default 400); mains uses gauss(blog_full_days, 2%). Replaced blog_voltage_empty/range config with blog_full_days/bemd_full_days. Both ports; validated.

title: callbackUrl emitted under wrong key (schema field is transferCallbackUrl)
description: Both ports emit meta.callbackUrl (utils/schemas.py:22 TransferMetadata.callbackUrl; utils/generator.py:16; js/src/schemas.js & device.js). The cce-interop-0.8.0 transmission-metadata schema names the webhook field 'transferCallbackUrl' (line 511). Because meta has additionalProperties:true and transferCallbackUrl is not required, this does NOT cause a 422 — but the supplied URL is silently unrecognized by the validator/consumer. CAUTION: schema types transferCallbackUrl as a non-nullable string, so simply renaming and emitting null would FAIL; emit the key only when a URL is present (omit otherwise). Applies to both Python and JS ports.
acceptance_criteria: When a callback URL is provided it is emitted as meta.transferCallbackUrl (string); when absent the key is omitted entirely (not null). No 'callbackUrl' key remains.
close_reason: Webhook field renamed callbackUrl -> transferCallbackUrl per cce-interop; typed non-nullable string and emitted only when a URL is present (omitted otherwise, never null). Both ports (schemas.py/generator.py, schemas.js/device.js). Verified key present when supplied, absent when not.

title: SVA (mains) emits supply voltage instead of voltage-availability seconds
description: utils/simulator/power.py:84 sets 'SVA': sva where sva = config.nominal_voltage (~230). Schema SVA ('AC Supply voltage availability') is the number of SECONDS within each 15-min period that AC voltage was in-bounds, range 0-900. Emitting ~230 passes the 0-900 range by coincidence (no 422), but the modeled quantity is wrong — it should be ~900 when powered, 0 during an outage. Appears to be a value mix-up with ACCD: the seconds value (powered_s) was placed in ACCD while the voltage landed in SVA (ACSV correctly carries voltage). Fix alongside the ACCD/DCCD current fix (ccesim-bua).
acceptance_criteria: SVA reflects in-bounds AC supply seconds (0-900) for the interval — e.g. full interval seconds when powered, 0 during outage — not the supply voltage.
close_reason: SVA now emits in-bounds AC seconds (int, 0-900): full interval when powered, 0 during outage -- not the supply voltage. ACSV keeps the voltage (uses nominal directly). Both ports; rng.gauss call count unchanged (no desync). Schema-validates over 200 records.

title: Locust: split oversized payloads to honor §1.4 1MB cap
description:
The Locust delivery POST currently sends one report per request and only emits a [WARN] when the post-compression body exceeds the spec §1.4 1MB cap (MAX_BODY_BYTES in locustfile.py) — it does not split. This is fine today (single report per POST stays well under 1MB), but becomes a real gap if/when batching multiple reports per POST is added (data=[report1, report2, ...]). 

Implement payload splitting: when a batch would exceed 1MB measured AFTER content-encoding (gzip), split the data array across multiple POSTs so each request body stays within the cap. Measure on the compressed bytes (§1.4 says 'after any applicable content encoding'). Until batching exists, the current WARN guard is the placeholder.
acceptance_criteria: When a batched payload would exceed 1MB after gzip, reports are split across multiple POSTs each <=1MB on the wire; single-report POSTs are unaffected. No silent truncation.

title: cce-interop-0.8.0 schema TCON/TCON2 example '101.50.3' is not a valid number
description: The cce-interop JSON schema (docs-2to8-cc/docs/cce-data-interop/schemas/cce-interop-0.8.0.json, $defs/PQS-DS01-objects/TCON and TCON2) declares type number (range -55..150) but lists examples: ['101.50.3'] -- a string with two decimal points, which is not a valid JSON number and does not conform to the object's own type. The authoritative PQS E006 DS01.2 Annex-1 defines TCON/TCON2 (condenser temperature) as Numeric, Data Format 000.0 (1 dp), -55..150 C. FIX: replace the malformed example with a valid 1-dp numeric in range, e.g. 101.5.
acceptance_criteria: cce-interop-0.8.0.json TCON and TCON2 examples are valid numbers within -55..150 at 1 dp precision.
close_reason: Replaced malformed TCON/TCON2 example '101.50.3' with valid 1-dp number 101.5 in cce-interop-0.8.0.json; validated JSON parses and examples conform (numeric, -55..150, 1dp). Matches Annex-1 format 000.0 and sibling numeric-object convention. Committed in docs-2to8-cc.

title: ACCD floored to 0.01 A during mains outage/idle, misrepresenting true zero draw
description: During a mains outage (and whenever the compressor is idle) the appliance draws no AC current, but ACCD is floored to the schema minimum 0.01 A (utils/simulator/power.py:94 max(0.01,...); js/src/power.js:114). This was done to satisfy the cce-interop ACCD minimum of 0.01, but it contradicts the co-emitted outage state (SVA=0 / ACSV=0) and the PQS Annex, which gives ACCD min value 0. The result reports 0.01 A being drawn while power is unavailable. Note the schema-vs-Annex conflict on the minimum (schema 0.01 vs Annex 0); decide whether outage/idle ACCD should be 0 (Annex) or remain floored, and reconcile. Low priority. Applies to both Python and JS.
acceptance_criteria: ACCD during a mains outage/no-draw condition is consistent with the power state (0 A per Annex, or an agreed reconciliation of the schema's 0.01 minimum), not a misleading 0.01 A draw.
close_reason: ACCD floor changed 0.01->0 during outage/no-draw (both ports). Authoritative PQS E006 DS01.2 Annex-1 sets ACCD Min Value=0 (Data Format 00.00); the schema's 0.01 was an over-tightening. Per Annex review with user, simulator now emits 0 A. Schema-side fix (min 0.01->0) tracked in ccesim-8yq. Supersedes ccesim-fuq's 'floor to 0.01' acceptance text.

title: DCCD rounded to 2 decimals; Annex Data Format for DCCD is 00.0 (1 decimal)
description: DC current DCCD is rounded to 2 decimal places (utils/simulator/power.py:175 round(...,2); js/src/power.js:216 round2). The PQS Annex Data Objects sheet specifies DCCD Data Format '00.0' (1 decimal place, range 0-99.9), whereas ACCD is '00.00' (2 dp, range 0-50) which the code rounds correctly. The bare JSON schema only bounds min/max (no precision constraint) so this won't 422, but it deviates from the Annex precision spec. Round DCCD to 1 decimal. Applies to both Python and JS.
acceptance_criteria: DCCD is emitted with 1 decimal place (matching Annex format 00.0); ACCD remains 2 decimals.
close_reason: DCCD rounded to 1 decimal (round1) to match Annex Data Format '00.0'; ACCD stays 2 dp ('00.00'). Both ports + tests strengthened to distinguish 1dp vs 2dp (raw 4.8667 -> 4.9).
